title: Listening contacts never compose, and a shared chain carries the far ring only after crossing the middle ring
subject: What a chain of three rings joined by two contacts can carry, read with the canonical knot test on its space-time law
conclusion: In a chain of three rings, listening contacts, which read their rings and feed nothing back, never let the far contact depend on the far ring, so composition needs a contact the middle ring reads. With shared contacts the far contact cannot depend on the first ring before lag d + 1, d the contacts' distance on the middle ring, and with linear or affine rules a contact binds two rings exactly when its row of M^T meets both.
